To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cells of intact rat liver have a higher yield of spontaneous and induced mutations than the cells of regenerating liver; the yield of polylploidy in the cells of regenerative rat liver is higher than in the cells of the resting liver; and the yield of poliploidy is higher in the cells of irradiated regenerative rat liver than in the cells in irradiated intact liver.
the cells of intact liver are characterized by a low level of polyploidy and a low yield of polyploids following radiation exposure.

the yield of spontaneous and induced genome mutation in cells of the liver of intact rats and rats with regenerating liver was compared, and that polyploidy was found to play a significant role in the ontogeny of the liver and during regeneration after its partial resection, and that the radiation sensitivity of cells in the regenerating liver was found to be lower than that in the intact liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of polyploidization in liver regeneration and with the radiation response of regenerating and intact cells of the liver.

the study of the effect of gamma irradiation on the yield of spontaneous and induced genome mutations and polyploidy, the frequency of which is higher in the regenerating than in the resting liver cells.
the role of the polyploidy process in the development of liver tissue and in the regeneration after partial hepatic resection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cells of regenerating liver are more resistant to the action of radiation than those of intact liver.
polyploidy is a normal process in the development and regeneration of liver, and that the polyploidization is a factor which contributes to the radiation response of liver cells.
the radiation response of regenerating cells is characterized by an enhanced radiosensitivity and a higher rate of recovery from the radiation effects as compared to that of resting cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the radiation response of the cells of the liver of intact and regening animals is determined by their different proliferative activity and by the peculiarities in the processes of repair of radiation damage in the resting and actively proliferating cells.

the yield of poliploid cells in the liver cells of intact and of regenerating liver after irradiation is determined by the balance between the processes of repair, fixation and elimination of the damages.
the radiation response of regenerating liver cells is determined by the peculiarities of the processes of DNA repair and fixation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiation response of liver cells depends on their proliferative state.
the cells of regenerating liver have a high capacity for polyploidization, and that the radiation-induced polyploidy is more pronounced in the resting liver cells.

the yield of polylpoidies is a sensitive indicator of the state of the genome of the cells and can be used for the evaluation of the effectiveness of the radiation response in different types of cells.
